result.reason: The New York governing-law language matches the preferred position, but the exclusive New York court-jurisdiction provision conflicts with the existing requirement that Disputes be resolved by binding arbitration. The redline should distinguish arbitration from court proceedings supporting or enforcing arbitration. Specifying New York County as the arbitral seat also changes the arbitration arrangement beyond what the playbook expressly requires. These changes create ambiguity and alter unrelated dispute-resolution terms rather than making a targeted governing-law and venue revision.
